source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 193: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 193: do not choose tensor parallelism (TP) or pipeline parallelism (PP) from the label alone; first establish feasibility and measure the actual service. Assume the model graph and layer shapes, precision, parameter/optimizer/activation memory, GPU count/type and usable HBM in GiB, topology and link bandwidth, software versions, clocks, request-length and arrival distributions, concurrency, batching policy, and latency, throughput, error, quality, and availability SLOs are recorded. Treat unknown platform values as estimates and report them as such. Enumerate feasible TP degrees and PP stage partitions. For each, calculate per-GPU memory headroom and measure compute time, collective/activation-transfer time, synchronization wait, pipeline bubble fraction, queueing, throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, error rate, output-quality checks, and reconfiguration/failure recovery time in stated units. TP shards tensors and can reduce memory per GPU, but adds frequent collectives whose cost depends on message size, topology, synchronization, and stragglers. PP reduces some collectives by partitioning layers, but needs balanced stage memory/compute, activation transfers, enough microbatches, and incurs bubbles and queueing; batch and microbatch choices must be held explicit. Pre-register a falsifiable hypothesis before tuning: at the target offered load and fixed SLO gates, the selected configuration improves held-out end-to-end p99 by at least a predefined M ms or M% over the best feasible alternative without violating p50, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, error, quality, or availability limits. Randomize repeated paired trials across configurations, use disjoint tuning and held-out request traces, warm up equally, and control model version, precision, clocks, topology, batch limits, arrival seed, background load, and failure state; report confidence intervals and all raw aggregates. Prefer the configuration only if memory headroom is positive and reliability gates pass. If neither wins, retain the current safe configuration and mark evidence_required. Test failure/recovery only in an authorized isolated environment with bounded fault injection, timeout, checkpoint/state-integrity and replica-health checks; never disrupt production or expose data. Define rollback triggers for OOM, hang, quality regression, error/availability breach, tail-latency regression, or failed recovery, with a versioned prior deployment and traffic drain/restore plan. A priori M and SLO thresholds, actual measurements, and domain-expert review are required before treating this provisional recommendation as authoritative.
risks: No platform measurements, SLO thresholds, workload trace, or topology facts are supplied; TP/PP preference cannot be asserted yet.
Tail latency and pipeline behavior are sensitive to load, microbatching, stage imbalance, collectives, and confounders.
Failure testing or reconfiguration can cause service disruption or state/quality regressions if not isolated and authorized.
evidence_required: Per-GPU memory and headroom by configuration in GiB
Topology-aware communication and activation-transfer timings
Repeated randomized paired trials with held-out p50/p95/p99, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, errors, quality, and availability
Authorized isolated recovery test and rollback rehearsal
Domain-expert review
